title: cert-manager-edit no longer lets namespace users create Challenges or Orders

detection.reason: the agent projects only the pod-subresource rules of a ClusterRole, so which API groups cert-manager-edit grants cannot be read; and tooling that creates Challenge or Order objects directly may not live on this cluster at all

quote: Starting in v1.20.3, the `cert-manager-edit` aggregate ClusterRole no longer grants `create` for `challenges.acme.cert-manager.io` or `create`, `patch`, `update` for `orders.acme.cert-manager.io`. This fixes a security issue (`GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258`) where these permissions allowed namespace users to bypass Issuer solver selectors and abuse ClusterIssuer credentials.
remediation: If any tooling creates Challenge or Order resources directly — outside the normal Certificate → CertificateRequest → Order → Challenge flow — grant it those permissions explicitly. This closed a security issue (GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258) and is not being reverted.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterrole cert-manager-edit -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.rules[] | select(.apiGroups[]? | test("acme.cert-manager.io")) | "\(.resources | join(",")): \(.verbs | join(","))"'  # create on challenges, and create/patch/update on orders, are what the upgrade removes
coversNotes: Restrict Challenge and Order RBAC in `cert-manager-edit` ClusterRole
